Plaek Phibunsongkhram, known as Phibun, was an army officer who led Thailand from 1938 to 1944 and again from 1948 to 1957. In 1939 he renamed Siam as Thailand.

A leader of the 1932 revolution, he admired the strongmen of Europe and Japan. His cultural mandates told Thais to wear Western hats, salute the flag and speak central Thai; his government promoted pad thai as a national dish.

He allied Thailand with Japan in 1941 and declared war on Britain and the United States. After the war he returned by coup and turned to the US in the Cold War. A coup in 1957 drove him into exile in Japan. See Thailand.
sum: Plaek Phibunsongkhram, known as Phibun, was an army officer who led Thailand from 1938 to 1944 and again from 1948 to 1957. In 1939 he renamed Siam as Thailand.
